title: NVLink traffic impact on paged vs flash attention: experiment notes
content:
Summary:

Quick experiment log exploring whether NVLink interconnect utilization explains intermittent tail-latency spikes we see when serving models with cross-GPU KV-caching (paged attention path) vs the FlashAttention path (local-GPU preference). High-level finding: NVLink traffic correlates strongly with 95/99p latency spikes for paged-attn when long-sequence requests cause remote KV fetches; FlashAttention suffers fewer NVLink transfers but shows different microbursts tied to kernel handoffs.

Background / Why we did this:
- Running multi-GPU inference with sharded KV cache (paged attention) to support very long contexts and memory-constrained GPUs.
- We observed occasional 200-600 ms tail spikes on A100 nodes serving mixed short/long sequences, not explained by GPU occupancy or host CPU load.
- Hypothesis: remote KV fetches traverse NVLink (or PCIe fallback), and NVLink congestion (especially cross-socket multi-job colocations) introduces queuing that manifests as tail latency. FlashAttention path keeps most data local, so it should be more robust, but kernel switch overheads and small-batch stuttering still exist.

Experiment setup (hardware + software):
- Cluster: 4x NVIDIA A100-SXM4 per server, NVSwitch-enabled, node has 3 other collocated benchmark jobs in some runs to simulate noisy neighbor NVLink traffic.
- Serving binary: rwinf-serving v0.63 (feature/kv-paged-prefetch branch).
- FlashAttention: flashattn v2.2 patched with fusedops from internal repo.
- Paged-attn shim: host pinned memory region + RDMA-like transfer simulated via p2p copies over NVLink.
- Traces: nsys (5.4) perf counters, nvlink counters via nvidia-smi dmon + custom nvlink sniffer (kernel module log).
- Workload: two mixes: (A) bursty mix: 80% short (32 tokens) / 20% long (4096 tokens) arrive Poisson, (B) uniform long (4096 tokens) steady. Batch size = dynamic (up to 8), concurrency 64.

Measurements captured:
- Per-request latency (p50/p95/p99) at gateway, per-kernel durations from nsys, NVLink TX/RX utilization traces, PCIe fallback counts, host <-> GPU memcpy durations, queue depths for async p2p streams.
- Synthetic counters: remote_kv_bytes, remote_kv_roundtrips, prefetch_hit_rate.

Key observations (top-level):
1) Paged-attn: 95/99p latency spikes line up with short bursts of very high NVLink utilization (90%+ on specific NVSwitch paths) and simultaneous increase in remote_kv_roundtrips. The pattern: a small number of long requests trigger large KV fetches that saturate NVLink, then many short concurrent requests (which need only local KV) are stalled due to NVLink cross-traffic in the same GPU interconnect fabric.
2) FlashAttention: average latencies lower by ~12-18% in mix A, and p95/p99 far less volatile. However, microbursts (~20-40 ms) persisted attributed to kernel handoffs when sequence lengths hop between small and large, causing fusion to be re-evaluated and causing short schedule pauses.
3) PCIe fallback: when NVLink saturation is deliberately simulated (we ran a synthetic NVLink saturator job), some remote transfers fell back to PCIe and those requests saw catastrophic latencies (2x-5x).
4) Prefetching behavior: our current prefetch window (prefetch next K tokens) is too conservative for high-seq variance workloads; prefetch misses generate on-demand NVLink transfers that pile up. Increasing prefetch window reduced tail by ~25% but raised average bandwidth usage ~30%.

Detailed trace notes (sanitized):
- Example trace (run 2024-12-11-14:03): 5 concurrent long requests triggered 1.2 GiB remote KV transfer across NVSwitch port 2-3 over 120 ms. During that 120 ms window p99 jumped from 160 ms to 520 ms for unrelated short requests. Nsys shows these remote memcpy operations blocking the async stream CH0 and CH3, kernel dispatch queues back up.
- Kernel timing: fused-attention kernel time dominated for long requests; but the blocking memcpy before kernel launch introduces queueing.
- NVLink counters show high packet retransmit-like metrics (driver reported link errors) for the busiest runs; worth engaging infra to check firmware.

Hypotheses we tried to validate (and preliminary verdicts):
- H1: NVLink saturation from remote KV fetches is primary cause of observed spikes. Verdict: supported by strong temporal correlation in most runs.
- H2: Prefetch window too small leads to reactive transfers. Verdict: supported; expanding window reduces remote roundtrip frequency but increases steady-state NVLink use.
- H3: FlashAttention microbursts are due to fusion decision recomputation. Verdict: partially supported; adding a cheap cache for fusion decisions eliminated ~60% of those short pauses in microbench.

Quick perf knobs tested and results (numbers are approximate):
- Increase prefetch from 128 KB to 2 MB per KV group: p99 reduced by 23% on mix A, but NVLink avg bandwidth +34%.
- Limit concurrent remote roundtrips to 4 per GPU (throttle queue): reduced p99 spikes but increased p50 by ~8% (queuing at serving layer).
- Co-locate KV shards on same NVSwitch fabric (affinity): reduced cross-switch transfers and improved tail by ~30%.
- Bundle small remote transfers into fewer large transfers (aggregation): headroom improved, p95 improved but implementation complexity high.

Unresolved anomalies / questions to follow up:
- Driver-level link error counts spiking in 2 runs (12/02 and 12/11). Need infra to check NVSwitch firmware and cabling (or driver bug).
- We still see rare ~300 ms spikes even with throttling; need to check host NIC interrupts and CUDA stream preemption interactions.
- How does behavior differ on DGX-style NVSwitch topology vs single NVLink chain? We have limited test beds for that.

Action items (next steps):
- [Infra] Open ticket with infra to validate NVSwitch firmware and check any recent kernel/driver patches (JIRA-RT-1889 created). Owner: Ritika. Due: 2025-01-17.
- [Engineering] Implement a prototype aggregated-remote-transfer path in serving-runtime to batch small KV fetches into fewer NVLink transactions. Owner: Marco. RFC PR by 2025-01-24.
- [Experiment] Run dedicated isolated runs on NVSwitch-only topology (no collocated jobs) and rerun mix A/B to quantify noisy-neighbor effect. Owner: Samir. Start 2025-01-13.
- [Runtime] Add fast-path cache for fusion-decision lookups in FlashAttention path to avoid recomputing heuristics on sequence-length changes. Owner: Aisha. Micropatch draft due 2025-01-20.
- [Monitoring] Expose remote_kv_roundtrips, nvlink_tx_util, and prefetch_miss_rate to console dashboards and add alert rule for sustained nvlink_tx_util > 75% for 30s. Owner: Observability team.

Short checklist for reproducing the core experiment locally (dev notes):
- checkout feature/kv-paged-prefetch; pip install -e .; build flashattn patched wheel via scripts/build_flashattn.sh
- run: ./bench/run_serving_bench.sh --nodes 1 --gpus 4 --concurrency 64 --mix bursty --trace nsys --out /tmp/nvlink-trace
- nvtop / nvidia-smi dmon during run to watch NVLink ports; capture /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/*/nvlink if available

Informal notes / anecdotes:
- Observed one run where a colocated model training job accidentally saturated NVSwitch during our bench and the tail latency jumped to near-10s for some requests. This is the classic noisy neighbor we are trying to tame with throttles and better affinity.
- Prefetch tuning is a tradeoff: larger windows reduce tail latency at cost of more NVLink spend — economics team should weigh cost vs SLA.

Conclusion (working):
Paged-attention introduces significant NVLink traffic that can materially affect tail latency under realistic mixed traffic patterns. FlashAttention avoids a lot of those transfers and presents a cleaner tail but has its own microburst failure modes tied to fusion decisions. Short-term wins: increase prefetch window modestly, add transfer aggregation, and throttle concurrent remote roundtrips. Mid-term: topology-aware placement + runtime aggregation and fusion-decision caches.

References & bookmarks:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/482 (kv-paged-prefetch)
- JIRA-RT-1889 (NVSwitch firmware/infra check)
- Confluence draft: confluence:redwood/attn-nvlink-traffic-notes

Notes-to-self: pack trace snippets into ticket, attach nsys timelines, push aggregated transfer patch as experimental feature flag so we can A/B test on Dedicated nodes.
